ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are a total of 6 black dots, arranged into upper and lower two horizontal rows, with 3 dots in each row. Reasoning: Using any 3 dots as vertices, first calculate all selection methods; there are C(6,3)=20 groups in total. When three points are collinear, they cannot form a triangle. Therefore the number of different triangles that can be formed is 20-2=18.

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram: there are 6 dots arranged as 2 horizontal rows with 3 dots in each row. The task asks for the number of distinct triangles using any 3 dots as vertices. Count all possible triples of dots: C(6,3)=20. Then exclude triples that do not form triangles because the three chosen dots are collinear. In the image, the only collinear triples are the 3 dots in the top row and the 3 dots in the bottom row, so subtract 2. Thus the number of triangles is 20-2=18.
